pages.title: Specifications
pages.llmsDescription: Navigable index of all SpecScore specifications with status and one-line descriptions.

pages.title: Feature Specification
pages.llmsDescription: The atomic unit of product specification. Defines directory structure, metadata (status, source ideas, grade), required sections, lifecycle, and adherence-footer conventions for Features.

pages.title: Plan Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Planning documents that bridge Feature specs to execution. Covers affected features, scope, approval workflow, and plan-level status.

pages.title: Task Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Discrete units of work within a Plan. Defines Task structure, fields, and how Tasks trace back to Plan scope.

pages.title: Acceptance Criteria Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Composite verification conditions (AC blocks) that bundle related Requirements inside a Feature's Acceptance Criteria section.

pages.title: Asking Good Questions for Good Specs
pages.llmsDescription: How to question a fuzzy request into complete, unambiguous, verifiable acceptance criteria — the question checklist, sharpening techniques, anti-patterns, and the test of a good spec.

pages.title: Explained by example: a login feature
pages.llmsDescription: One login feature walked through SpecScore's full artifact model — Idea (and a draft sibling), nested Features tree, Decision, Change Request/proposal, thin ACs, and Rehearse proof.

pages.title: Writing and Migrating Lessons
pages.llmsDescription: How to write compact process-improvement Lessons, add bounded occurrence evidence, and migrate legacy lesson files without losing history.

pages.title: Repo Config
pages.llmsDescription: Repo-level SpecScore configuration in `specscore.yaml` — project identity, modules, studio settings, publication policy, related projects.

pages.title: Source References Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Code-to-spec traceability via inline annotations. Every implemented requirement links back to the REQ or AC it satisfies.

pages.title: Decision Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) adapted to SpecScore conventions. Durable, lintable records of choices made between options — immutable once accepted, superseded never rewritten.

pages.title: Decisions Index Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Canonical index of active Decision documents in a repo. Inherits the shared Index shape with decisions-specific column set and numeric ordering.

pages.title: Lesson Specification
pages.llmsDescription: Durable process-improvement rules with append-only, bounded occurrence evidence and a Recorded → Stated → Enforced ladder.

pages.title: Rule Specification
pages.llmsDescription: How to write a Rule: one normative MUST/NEVER sentence with its scope grammar, enforcement ladder and required control, typed sources, the inline-versus-detailed two-form model, and reciprocity with Lessons and agent skills.

pages.title: Rules Index Specification
pages.llmsDescription: The rules index is both the inventory and the primary artifact: an inline Rule is one row and nothing else, the row stays authoritative for a detailed Rule, and a row that does not parse is preserved rather than dropped.

pages.title: Documentation
pages.llmsDescription: Documentation index — links to all specification pages, CLI install, AI plugins, and role-specific guides.

pages.title: Rehearse — in plain language
pages.llmsDescription: Plain-language explanation of Rehearse, SpecScore's acceptance-evidence layer: what it does, how scenarios run, what it deliberately does not do, and why.

pages.title: Rehearse vs. Established Testing Frameworks
pages.llmsDescription: Why Rehearse is not a pytest/go-test rival but an acceptance-evidence layer: differences from Cucumber (no step-definition glue), honest limitations, and when to use it.

pages.title: Entities and Properties
pages.llmsDescription: Author guide for the entity and property Doc-Kinds — typed business data with YAML-frontmatter source of truth, ref-based property reuse, and additive-only inheritance.
